newsitem.title: CHINA: China's currency seen slightly stronger in Q4.
newsitem.headline: China's currency seen slightly stronger in Q4.

text.p: China's currency is seen growing stronger to the end of the year on rising exports and falling inflation, said an edition of the Business News seen in Beijing on Sunday.
Faster payment of export tax rebates had helped to fuel a rise in exports, bringing in more foreign exchange and buoying the yuan, the newspaper said in its November 27 edition.
The supply of foreign exchange far exceeded demand, the newspaper quoted analysts from the China Foreign Exchange Trade System as saying.
Interest rate cuts in May and August would not cause a great outflow of foreign currency or put downward pressure on the yuan, the analysts said.
A tight monetary policy and not-too-rapid economic growth would continue to support the stability of the yuan, they said but did not elaborate.
Beijing announced it would make the yuan covertible under the current account on December 1.
China's foreign exchange reserves were $100.45 billion as of November 12 while retail price inflation rose a year-on-year 4.7 percent in October compared with 14.8 percent for all of 1995.
